Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer with its own UI under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Users often ask the in-app AI how to use a feature, and the AI had nothing describing JusPrin's own screens. On 2026-11-11 a first guide page was written and a pre-release process built for it, on branch `claude/app-guide` (commit a05657617b, pushed to origin; another session's worktree is at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin-worktrees/app-guide`, do not work in that folder).

What exists on that branch:
- `docs/guide/print-settings.md` is the one guide page so far, read by people on GitHub. `docs/guide/README.md` is the index and describes the process. Five pictures are in `docs/guide/pictures/print-settings/` (about 400 KB together), taken from the built app by the shell harness.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds the skill the AI reads (`skills/guide-print-settings/SKILL.md`) from the page. A page starts with `<!-- ai-description: … -->`, holds AI-only notes in `<!-- ai: … -->`, and uses bold only for on-screen labels.
- `guide.test.ts` beside it checks labels, sections, pictures and questions. `scripts/check_guide.py` is the one command run before a release.

Kenneth's decisions so far: the guide serves both people and the AI; SEO is set aside; he wants the process simple, his words being "I don't want it to be too complicated and fancy. What I need is that the document can be brought in sync with the code before we make another release." Earlier he chose that people read the guide on GitHub first and an in-app Help window comes later. On 2026-11-11, in a side conversation, he decided to build the in-app window now, with search, and said he will set this task's options himself before starting it. The window replaces the earlier plan of a Help menu item that opens the guide on GitHub.

Kenneth's communication rules are in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and the project's in `AGENTS.md`: full sentences, no invented labels, proposals marked as proposals, decisions asked in full, outcomes reported with what was tested.

Task:
Build a Help window inside JusPrin that lets a person search the app guide and read a guide page with its pictures. Everything below about how to build it is a proposal from an earlier conversation, not a settled design; Kenneth may have set different options when starting this task, and his instructions win.

The proposal:
- A Help menu item, with wording such as "JusPrin guide…", in JusPrin's Help menu: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/AppMenus.cpp`, `build_help`, beside "Ask AI…" and "Report a problem…".
- It opens a native window that shows one more page of the AgentUI bundle, the way the Preferences window (`?panel=preferences`) and the import window (`?panel=orca-import`) do. See `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/main.tsx`, `PreferencesApp.tsx`, `OrcaImportApp.tsx`, and the native windows `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Preferences/PreferencesWindow.cpp` and `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaImportWindow.cpp`.
- The page lists the guide pages from `docs/guide`, has a search box that narrows to the sections matching the typed words (plain matching over headings and text, no search index), and shows a page with its pictures. The bundle already renders Markdown with `react-markdown` (`components/MarkdownMessage.tsx`, which deliberately makes links and images inert in chat replies; a guide page needs its own rendering that shows the guide's own pictures).

Open points to settle, by measuring or by asking Kenneth in full:
- Pictures. The page is built as one file (`vite-plugin-singlefile`), so pictures would be packed into it. One guide page's five pictures are about 400 KB. Whether to pack them or ship them as separate resource files is undecided and unmeasured. Measure the bundle size both ways before choosing.
- Design. The project's rule is whole-screen boards with real text before code: read `agent-docs/jusprin/design-guidelines.md` and "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` first. Every colour, radius, font and control size comes from the token file. Expect design to be the largest part.
- Only one guide page exists (print settings). The window must work with one page and with the seven that are planned.
- Not verified: whether the Mac's system search field appears in JusPrin's Help menu, and how much of the Preferences window code a Help window can reuse.
- The guide's AI-only parts (`<!-- ai-description -->`, `<!-- ai: -->`) must not show in the window.
- `guide.test.ts` and `scripts/check_guide.py` should keep covering what the window shows, so the window cannot drift from the pages.

Rules of the repository that apply: read `AGENTS.md` and `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` first. Make your own worktree and build; do not use `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin-worktrees/app-guide`. Builds on this shared Mac use `-j4`, one build per build folder, and reuse the dependencies as `AGENTS.md` describes. On-screen strings follow the translation rules in `AGENTS.md`. Do not open a pull request or merge unless Kenneth asks.

Done looks like: in the built app, Help has the new item; choosing it opens the window; typing in the search box narrows to matching sections; opening a result shows the page with its pictures; the AgentUI tests and the type check pass; you have looked at the window in the running app, in light and dark, and can show Kenneth screenshots of it. Report what you built, what you tested and the result, and what is still open.

# JusPrin guide

How to use JusPrin, one page per part of the app.

- [Seeing and changing print settings](print-settings.md)

## Before a release

The guide is brought in line with the app before each release, on a computer with the app built.

1. Build the app's test harness and pages from the commit to release: the `shell_integration_harness` and `jusprin_web` targets.
2. Leave the computer alone and run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. It takes about a minute a page, plus the questions.
3. Fix what it reports, then run it again until it passes:
   - **A label is on no screen.** The app's wording changed. Find the new wording in the app and correct the page.
   - **A run failed.** Open its log, which the command names. Either the screen no longer works as the page says, and the page needs correcting, or the harness expects something the app no longer does, and the harness needs correcting.
   - **A picture is blank.** The program that started the command may not record the screen. Grant it Screen Recording in the system's privacy settings and run again.
   - **AI answered a question wrongly.** Read its reply in the output. Usually the page is unclear or its first line does not say when to read it.
4. Look through what changed on screen since the last release (`git log <last release tag>..HEAD -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin`). The command finds what a page gets wrong. It cannot find a new screen or menu item that no page mentions, so add those by hand.
5. Commit the pages together with their pictures and the skills the command rebuilt.

## What the command does

1. **Walks the app and takes the pictures.** `tests/shell/guide_checks.json` names, for each page, the runs of the app's test harness that go through the screens the page describes, and the checks in each run the page depends on. `tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py` runs them in the app as built and copies the pictures a page uses into `pictures/<page>/`.
2. **Rebuilds the copy AI reads.** `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds a skill from each page.
3. **Checks each page**, in `guide.test.ts` beside it: every label in bold is in the app's source, every section has a run in step 1, every picture is one step 1 took, and the page has questions for step 4.
4. **Asks AI the page's questions** (`--ask-ai`). `tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json` holds them with what a right answer says. `tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py` asks the model and has a judge read the replies.

## Writing a page

- Start it with `<!-- ai-description: … -->`: one line, at most 300 bytes, saying when AI should read it.
- Put words that are only for AI in `<!-- ai: … -->`. They are hidden on this site.
- Use bold only for words that are on screen, exactly as they are on screen.
- A picture goes on a line of its own, as `![what it shows](pictures/<page>/<name>.png)`, and comes from a run named in `guide_checks.json`. AI's copy leaves it out.
- Give each `##` section a run in `guide_checks.json`.
- Add at least three questions for the page to `guide_questions.json`.
- AI's copy may hold at most 16 KiB. Split a page that grows past that.

# Seeing and changing print settings

Where the settings of a print are shown in JusPrin, and the ways to change them.

Names in bold are the words on screen. On a Mac the menus named here are in the menu bar. On Windows and Linux they are inside the menu at the left of the title bar.

<!-- ai: This guide is the by-hand route. When the person wants a setting changed and has not said they want to do it themselves, I change it with my settings tools. I give these steps when they ask where something is or want to do it themselves. -->

## See the settings a print will use

The **Setup summary** card at the top of the AI panel names the process and filament presets in use and says how many settings differ from them. If the AI panel is hidden, open the **View** menu and choose **Show AI panel** (on Windows and Linux, tick **AI panel**).

![The Setup summary card at the top of the AI panel, with the All settings link at its right](pictures/print-settings/setup-summary.png)

To see every setting:

1. On the Setup summary card, click **All settings**. The link is there once AI is set up.
2. Under **Showing**, pick **Whole project**, one plate, or one object. Plates are listed when the project has two or more. The list also follows what is selected in the 3D view.
3. Type in **Search settings** to find a setting by name, or switch from **All** to **Changed** to see only the settings that differ from the presets.
4. Click **Back to chat** to close the list.

![The All settings list, showing the whole project, with the Search settings box and the All and Changed switch](pictures/print-settings/all-settings.png)

The settings are grouped as Quality, Strength, Speed, Support, Multimaterial and Others, then Filament and Printer. The list is for reading: a value cannot be typed into it.

## Change a print setting

Print settings are things like layer height, infill, supports and speed. JusPrin's own view has no field to type them into. There are two ways to change one:

- Ask AI in the chat, for example "set the layer height to 0.16 mm". The change is then listed in the chat with the old and the new value.
- Switch to classic view, which has every print setting on screen. See [Classic view](#classic-view-every-setting-on-screen).

## Take a settings change back

- Each change made in a chat is listed in that chat. Point at a change and click the curved-arrow button at its right, named **Revert to here**. Then click **Revert to here** in the question that opens. The model and the project's settings go back to that point. The current model is saved in Version history first, and the chat, exported files and finished prints stay as they are.

![The Revert to here question over a list of changes in a chat](pictures/print-settings/revert-to-here.png)
- When a preset was saved from the chat, a line reading "Saved:" with the preset's name follows. Click **Undo** on that line to bring its earlier values back.
- To go back to an earlier state of the whole project, open the **File** menu and choose **Version history…**.

## Change printer or filament settings

These open a window with every setting of the printer or of a filament.

- Printer: click the printer's name in the header of the project, then **Printer settings…**. The **Printer** menu has the same item. With no printer chosen yet, it starts adding a printer.
- Filament: click the filament in the header of the project, then **Filament settings…**. With several filaments, pick one from the list first. The **Printer** menu has the same item for the first filament.

## Settings for one plate

1. In the **Plates** tab at the left, open the plate's "⋯" menu, or right-click the plate.
2. Choose **Plate settings…**.

![The Plates tab, with the ⋯ button at the right of a plate's row](pictures/print-settings/plates-tab.png)

The window holds what can differ per plate: the plate's name, its bed type, the print sequence, spiral vase, and the filament sequence of the first and the other layers. A setting made there shows in All settings with the note "Set on this plate".

## Settings for one object

An object can have settings of its own that differ from the project's. Its row in the **Plates** tab then carries a diamond mark, and the mark's menu says how many it has.

- To see them, open **All settings** and pick the object under **Showing**.
- To take one off, click **Use project value** on its row. A support blocker or enforcer has **Remove**.
- To add one or edit its value, ask AI in the chat, or use classic view.

![All settings showing one object, with Use project value beside its own Wall loops and Remove beside a support blocker](pictures/print-settings/object-settings.png)

## Classic view: every setting on screen

Classic view is the app's original screen, with all print settings in a panel at the side.

1. Open the **View** menu and choose **Switch to classic view…**. The "…" button in the header of the project has the same item.
2. A bar across the top says the window is in classic view. Click **Back to JusPrin** on it to return. The **View** menu also has **Switch to JusPrin view**.

// The app guide. Each docs/guide/<area>.md is a page a person reads on GitHub
// and the source of the skill the model reads: skills/guide-<area>/SKILL.md is
// built from it here and checked in, so everything that reads the skills
// folder (skills.ts, the app's tools test, the wording guard) takes it as any
// other skill. guide.test.ts fails when a page and its skill differ, and
// rewrites the skills when run with JUSPRIN_UPDATE_GUIDE_SKILLS=1.
//
// A page is written for the person. Three things in it are for the model:
// - its first line, <!-- ai-description: … -->, is the line skill_read lists;
// - <!-- ai: … --> holds a note only the model gets, hidden on the page;
// - a line that is only a picture is left out of the skill.

const DESCRIPTION = /^<!-- ai-description: (.+) -->\n/;
const AI_NOTE = /<!-- ai: ([\s\S]*?) -->/g;
const PICTURE_LINE = /^!\[[^\]]*\]\([^)]*\)\n/gm;
const LINK_WITHIN_PAGE = /\[([^\]]+)\]\(#[^)]*\)/g;

export function guideSkillFile(area: string, page: string): string {
  const text = page.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n');
  const description = text.match(DESCRIPTION);
  if (!description) throw new Error(`${area}: a guide page starts with <!-- ai-description: … -->`);
  const body = text.slice(description[0].length)
    .replace(PICTURE_LINE, '')
    .replace(AI_NOTE, '$1')
    .replace(LINK_WITHIN_PAGE, '$1')
    .replace(/\n{3,}/g, '\n\n')
    .trim();
  // Any other comment would reach the model as text.
  if (body.includes('<!--')) throw new Error(`${area}: only ai-description and ai comments are understood`);
  return `---\nname: guide-${area}\ndescription: ${description[1]}\n---\n\n${body}\n`;
}

// The on-screen words a page quotes: bold is kept for those alone.
export function guideLabels(page: string): string[] {
  return [...new Set([...page.matchAll(/\*\*([^*]+)\*\*/g)].map((match) => match[1]))];
}

// Whether `source` has `label` as a whole string or as a whole piece of page text.
export function hasLabel(source: string, label: string): boolean {
  const escaped = label.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
  return new RegExp(`["'\`>]\\s*${escaped}\\s*["'\`<]`).test(source);
}

// Keeps the app guide true to the app: each page's skill is the one built
// from it, and every on-screen label a page quotes is still in the source.
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { guideLabels, guideSkillFile, hasLabel } from './guide';
import { parseSkill } from './skillParser';

const src = __dirname;
const root = join(src, '../../../../../..');
const pages = join(root, 'docs/guide');
const areas = readdirSync(pages).filter((name) => name.endsWith('.md') && name !== 'README.md')
  .map((name) => name.slice(0, -3)).sort();
const page = (area: string) => readFileSync(join(pages, `${area}.md`), 'utf8');
const skillPath = (area: string) => join(src, 'skills', `guide-${area}`, 'SKILL.md');

function files(dir: string, wanted: RegExp): string[] {
  return readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((entry) => {
    const path = join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) return entry.name === 'node_modules' ? [] : files(path, wanted);
    return wanted.test(entry.name) && !/\.test\./.test(entry.name) ? [path] : [];
  });
}

// Everything that puts words on a screen: the native windows, the app's own
// and the ones it keeps, and the two pages.
const screens = files(join(root, 'src/slic3r/GUI'), /\.(cpp|hpp|tsx?)$/).map((path) => readFileSync(path, 'utf8')).join('\n');
const missingLabels = (text: string) => guideLabels(text).filter((label) => !hasLabel(screens, label));

describe('the app guide', () => {
  it('has a page', () => expect(areas).not.toEqual([]));

  it.each(areas)('%s: the skill the model reads is built from the page', (area) => {
    const built = guideSkillFile(area, page(area));
    if (process.env.JUSPRIN_UPDATE_GUIDE_SKILLS === '1') {
      mkdirSync(dirname(skillPath(area)), { recursive: true });
      writeFileSync(skillPath(area), built);
    }
    // Out of date: run this test with JUSPRIN_UPDATE_GUIDE_SKILLS=1.
    expect(existsSync(skillPath(area)) ? readFileSync(skillPath(area), 'utf8').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n') : '').toBe(built);
    // The limits the app holds a skill to: the description's and the text's size.
    expect(parseSkill(built, skillPath(area)).description).toBeTruthy();
  });

  it('has no guide skill without a page', () => {
    const built = readdirSync(join(src, 'skills')).filter((name) => name.startsWith('guide-')).sort();
    expect(built).toEqual(areas.map((area) => `guide-${area}`));
  });

  it.each(areas)('%s: every label it quotes is on a screen', (area) => {
    expect(missingLabels(page(area))).toEqual([]);
  });

  // tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py asks the model these: a page with
  // none is a page nobody has checked the model can answer from.
  it('has questions to ask the model about every page, and none about a page that is gone', () => {
    const questions = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json'), 'utf8')) as
      Record<string, { id: string; question: string; answer: string }[]>;
    expect(Object.keys(questions).sort()).toEqual(areas);
    for (const area of areas) expect(questions[area].length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);
  });

  // tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py runs these in the app as built and copies
  // their pictures into docs/guide/pictures. A section no run walks is a
  // section nobody has checked in the app.
  describe('against the running app', () => {
    const checks = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'tests/shell/guide_checks.json'), 'utf8')) as
      Record<string, { covers: string[]; args: string[]; pictures?: Record<string, string> }[]>;
    const sections = (area: string) => [...page(area).matchAll(/^## (.+)$/gm)].map((match) => match[1]);

    it('has harness runs for every page, and none for a page that is gone', () => {
      expect(Object.keys(checks).sort()).toEqual(areas);
    });

    it.each(areas)('%s: a run walks every section', (area) => {
      const covered = new Set(checks[area].flatMap((run) => run.covers));
      expect(sections(area).filter((section) => !covered.has(section))).toEqual([]);
      expect([...covered].filter((section) => !sections(area).includes(section))).toEqual([]);
    });

    it.each(areas)('%s: its pictures are the ones the runs take', (area) => {
      const used = [...page(area).matchAll(/^!\[[^\]]+\]\(pictures\/([^)]+)\)$/gm)].map((match) => match[1]).sort();
      const taken = checks[area].flatMap((run) => Object.keys(run.pictures ?? {})).map((name) => `${area}/${name}`).sort();
      expect(used).toEqual(taken);
      expect(used.filter((name) => !existsSync(join(pages, 'pictures', name)))).toEqual([]);
    });
  });

  it('notices a label no screen has, and a label that is only part of another', () => {
    expect(missingLabels('Click **No such button** and then **All settings**.')).toEqual(['No such button']);
    // "Switch to classic" is on no screen by itself; "Switch to classic view…" is.
    expect(missingLabels('**Switch to classic**')).toEqual(['Switch to classic']);
  });

  it('builds a skill from a page', () => {
    const built = guideSkillFile('some-area', [
      '<!-- ai-description: Read before saying where things are. -->', '', '# Some area', '',
      '![The window](pictures/window.png)', '', '<!-- ai: I can do this myself. -->', '',
      'See [the other part](#the-other-part).', '',
    ].join('\r\n'));
    expect(built).toBe('---\nname: guide-some-area\ndescription: Read before saying where things are.\n---\n\n'
      + '# Some area\n\nI can do this myself.\n\nSee the other part.\n');
    expect(() => guideSkillFile('bad', '# No description\n')).toThrow('ai-description');
    expect(() => guideSkillFile('bad', '<!-- ai-description: Fine. -->\n# Title\n<!-- todo -->\n')).toThrow('comments');
  });
});

# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-dev`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [Design guidelines](design-guidelines.md) — how a screen gets designed and checked, the cold-reader check, and the wording rule for on-screen text.
8. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
9. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
10. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Moonraker and OctoPrint without hardware (Docker, real host software, simulated boards): [print hosts README](../../tests/printer_hosts/README.md).

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). `jusprin-dev` continues `jusprin-newui` and `ui-walkthrough`: it starts at `975c703f08`, the merge of OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, and contains both. The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.

# JusPrin design guidelines

**Status:** Canonical guidance for `jusprin-dev` on how a screen gets designed and checked, and on the words it shows. The visual system (tokens, type, color, components, logo) lives in [Design system](design-system.md); this document does not repeat it.

Design agents tend to write on-screen text that only they can read. The agent knows how the screen works, so a line like "The sixth digit signs you in." reads clearly to it and to any reviewer who knows the same. A person opening the app for the first time has to decode it, and often can't. The First-Launch Confusion Review (https://claude.ai/artifact/91wmdS3QU8UkzbPi1zog15, 2026-11-06) found 23 places on the first launch where a newcomer would misread or stall, and most of them were wording. The rules below exist to stop that at the source and to catch what still gets through.

## How a screen gets designed and checked

These steps apply to every change to text a person sees, not only to new screens: a new link on an existing board, a reworded line, or a one-sentence fix all get the cold-reader check on the board before building (step 5) and in the running app after (step 8).

1. **Start from the person.** Before drawing, write down in two or three sentences who reaches this screen, what they know at that moment, what they came to do, and what they must decide here. Every line on the screen serves one of those.
2. **Draw the whole screen, not a component alone.** A board for review is the full screen at the app's size, with the header, panes and neighbouring content the person really sees there, on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). Build it from the Design System artifact's coded components and the app's own markup, never by copying an older board. Repeated compositions are imported by name, as [Design handoff requirements](design-system.md#design-handoff-requirements) rule 9 says.
3. **Fill it with real strings.** Text that summarises data comes from the rule that will produce it in the app, run on real data. If only a model could write a line, say so on the board.
4. **Write every line by the wording rule below.**
5. **Run the cold-reader check on the boards** (below). Rewrite and check again until every line and button reads as intended.
6. **Show the board for review by what a person sees.** Name the screen as the person would ("the welcome screen, after typing an email"), give the canvas page it is on, and attach the picture. Board ids and builder labels mean nothing to a reviewer.
7. **Build it** following [Writing UI code](design-system.md#writing-ui-code).
8. **Check it in the running app.** Take screenshots of the built screen along one real path and run the cold-reader check again. The guards prove the code went through the tokens; only the screenshots show what the person reads.

## The cold-reader check

The writer of a screen cannot see that its text is cryptic, so the check is done by a reader who knows nothing about how the screen works.

- Start a fresh agent. Give it only the screenshots and one or two sentences a real user would know (for example: "You own a 3D printer and just installed JusPrin, a desktop app that prepares 3D models for printing."). Give it no code, spec, design notes, chat history or list of suspected problems, and rename files so their names don't hint at anything.
- Use screenshots from one coherent path, in the order a person meets them. Mixing signed-in and signed-out screens, or states set by hand, makes the reader report contradictions that no user would see.
- Ask it, for each screen, to quote every line and every button exactly, say in one plain sentence what the line means or what the button will do, and list where it would hesitate, misread, worry, or not know what to do next, including information the screen leaves out. Tell it to read literally, like a busy newcomer: a line it had to puzzle out counts as a problem even if it worked it out.
- Compare its answers with the intent written in step 1. Any line it reads differently from the intent gets rewritten, however small the gap. Its other hesitations are input to weigh, not orders.

What the check is known to catch: on 2026-11-06 a fresh agent given only the review's ten screenshots fully caught 14 of the 23 problems and partly caught 4 more. It caught every cryptic phrasing in the list. It missed problems that need knowledge from outside the screen (that Skip installs a 250 mm Klipper printer) and finer editorial calls (a redundant reassurance, one allowance under three names, "Connected" used for an account). It also raised real questions the review had not, such as what happens after the free month. It has not been compared with a real first-time user, so for the screens that matter most, such as first launch, a person remains the final test.

## Wording

Every line says what the person does or what happens to them, in a full sentence, in words a newcomer already has.

The five patterns below are what the review found most. Each pair is the text the app showed and the review's proposed rewrite; the rewrites are proposals, not yet in the app.

1. **Facts joined by a middle dot.** The dot drops how the facts relate, and the reader guesses.
   - Before: "Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits" (reads like a balance the person already had)
   - After: "You got 500 free credits for signing up.", with the email address on a smaller line under it
2. **Metaphors.** The reader has to work out what the image stands for.
   - Before: "New or existing account, same door."
   - After: a "Sign up free" button, with "Already have an account? Sign in" under it
   - Before: "Pick how the agent should think." (the options are ways to pay for or connect the agent)
   - After: "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice."
3. **Describing the mechanism instead of the action.** Say what the person does, not how the screen works inside.
   - Before: "The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device."
   - After: "Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone."
4. **Internal labels.** A name the team uses, shown nowhere else on the screen, explains nothing.
   - Before: "An Expert message is 5 credits."
   - After: the cost in things the person does, for example "500 credits is about 100 questions to the agent" (check the number against real costs)
5. **Hinting at a consequence instead of stating it.** If a choice changes what the person gets, say what it changes.
   - Before: "Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours."
   - After: "If you skip, files are sliced for a stand-in printer with a 250 mm bed, not for yours. Add your printer before you print anything. You can do that later on the home screen."

Space on a screen is tight, and short text looks finished. That is how these lines get written. Shorten only after the full sentence passes the cold-reader check, and check again after shortening.

# JusPrin design system

**Status:** Canonical product and brand guidance for `jusprin-dev`.

JusPrin should make advanced 3D printing feel immediate: a confident path from model to machine that removes detours without hiding control. The product should feel focused, assured, inventive, and approachable. Its voice is direct, capable, and optimistic—never cute, cryptic, or over-engineered.

The JusPrin logo is a soft-serve cone, chosen on 2026-11-03 from the concepts on the JusPrin Logo Concepts canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/Qroq8EdcQDSPkCAyFceDtQ). It replaced the earlier star-and-ring mark, which is still in repository history at revision `6eecb78b19`. The purple gradient endpoints are the Orbit and Bloom tokens. Positioning language in the POC brand kit is proposed product direction, not an externally sourced market claim.

## Brand behavior

- **Focused:** every element earns its place.
- **Assured:** guidance is calm and actions are decisive.
- **Inventive:** the product is technical without being intimidating.
- **Approachable:** use plain language instead of slicer jargon where possible.
- Make the next action obvious. Brand behavior should feel as focused as the visual system.

The mark is a soft-serve swirl of four rounded print layers on a waffle cone, with a curl on top: 3D printing shown as something friendly. Beside it, the name is cut into the same layers (seven for capitals, five for small letters), and a small nozzle above the i is still printing its dot, the last layer. `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Brand/brand_logo.py` draws every logo file from this one geometry.

Write the name exactly as **JusPrin**: capital J and P, no space, never all caps in body copy. Use surrounding text color for the name in ordinary copy; do not force a gradient into small text.

## Logo use

The primary expressions are the horizontal lockup, the compact product mark, and the text wordmark. Use the compact mark for application icons and small product contexts.

- Clear space: at least one quarter of the mark width on every side.
- Minimum digital mark: 24 px.
- Minimum digital horizontal lockup: 120 px.
- Minimum printed mark: 8 mm.
- Minimum printed lockup: 32 mm.
- Below these sizes, use the mark alone and verify that the orbit arcs remain distinct.

Always use the original artwork, preserve its aspect ratio and components, maintain clear space, and place it on White, Mist, Ink, or another quiet solid field. Do not stretch, rotate, redraw, arbitrarily recolor, outline, shadow, separate, or place it directly over visual noise. Monochrome is allowed only when required. If the center crossing or orbit loses clarity, increase size, contrast, or space.

## Brand palette

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---:|---|
| Orbit | `#3A2D64` | Primary brand color and decisive light-mode action |
| Violet | `#6F4F84` | Secondary brand color, headings, and essential boundaries |
| Bloom | `#CE84B7` | Expressive accent and dark-mode primary action |
| Ink | `#17131F` | Primary text and dark canvas |
| Mist | `#F6F2F7` | Soft canvas and grouped surfaces |
| Trace | `#E8DFEB` | Light dividers and quiet structure |
| White | `#FFFFFF` | Primary light canvas |
| Success | `#2D6A55` | Light success state |
| Danger | `#B44757` | Light error or destructive state |
| Warning | `#D49A2A` | Light warning state |

The signature gradient runs from Orbit to Bloom. Reserve it for the logo mark, splash, onboarding, and rare hero moments. Do not use it as ordinary product chrome.

Product code must resolve colors through semantic tokens in `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; raw palette values are not a component API.

## Semantic color behavior

Dark mode is a semantic remapping, not a visual inversion. Preserve hierarchy, density, and geometry while choosing the dark value for the same named intent.

Core mappings include:

| Token | Light | Dark | Purpose |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `surface.canvas` | `#FFFFFF` | `#17131F` | Main application background |
| `surface.subtle` | `#F6F2F7` | `#211B2A` | Sidebars and grouped settings |
| `surface.raised` | `#FFFFFF` | `#2B2336` | Dialogs, menus, elevated panels |
| `surface.raisedHover` | `#F6F2F7` | `#3B3047` | The hovered or keyboard-focused row in a menu or popover |
| `text.primary` | `#17131F` | `#F6F2F7` | Headings, values, body copy |
| `text.secondary` | `#5F5767` | `#CFC5D3` | Descriptions and secondary labels |
| `border.subtle` | `#E8DFEB` | `#4B3E57` | Dividers and quiet structure |
| `border.strong` | `#6F4F84` | `#7D6A8D` | Focus and essential boundaries |
| `action.primary` | `#3A2D64` | `#CE84B7` | Decisive primary action |
| `action.primary.hover` | `#4B3A77` | `#D99AC5` | Pointer hover |
| `action.primary.pressed` | `#2B214F` | `#B76CA0` | Pressed or active state |

The JSON token file is authoritative for the code and contains the complete action, status, selected-surface, disabled, text, and component values. Every colour it shares with the design system holds the design system's value; `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` pins each one beside its design-system name. Secondary and danger buttons have no colours of their own: like the design system's Button/Secondary they have no fill, a `border.subtle` (secondary) or `status.danger` (danger) stroke, and `text.primary` or `status.danger` text, with `surface.subtle` on hover and `surface.selected` when pressed. `overlay.scrim` and `status.successOnAction` exist only in the code until the Design System artifact adds them.

## Typography

Product UI uses fonts already shipped by OrcaSlicer:

- HarmonyOS Sans SC Regular for body and controls.
- HarmonyOS Sans SC Bold for hierarchy and actions.
- NanumGothic for Korean and Sarabun for Thai where the existing application requires them.
- The system GUI font as fallback.
- The system monospace font only for code: API keys, file paths, commands, config text, and IDs such as hashes. Never for names, words, or measurements.

HarmonyOS Sans SC draws every digit at the same width, so times, percentages,
and other values that change in place do not shift in the UI face; they do
not need the monospace one. In the native shell only the About window's
build commit uses it, through `ShellTheme::code_font()`.

Never require Menlo or another platform-specific face. The broader marketing brand kit used Avenir Next for display and marketing; that is not the cross-platform product UI requirement.

| Role | Size/line height in DIP | Weight |
|---|---:|---|
| Page title | 24/30 | Bold |
| Section | 18/24 | Bold |
| Body and control | 14/20 | Regular |
| Body bold | 14/20 | Bold |
| Body small | 13/18 | Regular |
| Body small bold | 13/18 | Bold |
| Label | 12/16 | Regular |
| Label bold | 12/16 | Bold |
| Dense metadata | 10/14 | Regular |
| Dense metadata bold | 10/14 | Bold |
| Code (system monospace) | 12/16 | Regular |

The bold pairs exist for emphasis inside a run of the same size (a primary
action beside secondary ones, the current row of a menu, a chip's name beside
its detail). Code is a single role, `typography.code`, whatever size the
text around it is.

The Agent pane's conversation is read at Body: messages, reply choices, the
message box, and the text of the cards in the thread. Buttons are not: a
secondary button is Body Small at 32 DIP and a primary button Body Small Bold
at 34 DIP everywhere, the buttons of the cards in the thread included (decided
2026-10-27). Text that
supports it sits one step below: Body Small for card details, notes from
JusPrin and the setup card's lines, Label Bold for small card headings and the
setup card's eyebrow. The turn's activity line and timestamps are Metadata.
The chat list and the message box's pickers keep their own sizes (decided
2026-10-26).

## Layout and geometry

Design for a dense, native, high-DPI desktop application on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Use device-independent pixels (DIP), not physical pixels. Verify 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling.

- Spacing scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, and 48 DIP, plus a 2 DIP half step (`dimension.space["0.5"]`) used only for the gap between a row's main line and the detail line under it, as in a report finding or a canvas caption.
- The radius scale carries the design system's names (`dimension.radius`):
  - `small`, 4 DIP: standard controls (secondary and icon buttons, fields, the segmented control), matching OrcaSlicer's own controls.
  - `medium`, 8 DIP: containers (cards, popovers, chat bubbles) and the primary button, the one branded action.
  - `large`, 12 DIP: sheets, large dialogs and window actions.
  - `chip`, 4 DIP: the printer and filament chip in the header.
  - `full`, 14 DIP: capsule ends of anything up to 28 DIP tall: reply choices, status chips and progress tracks. A shorter box keeps a full capsule, because a radius larger than half the height is drawn as half of it.
- Menus follow the design system's Menu/Popover and Menu/Row: the popover has 8 DIP
  vertical padding, a 1 DIP border and 2 DIP between rows; rows are 36 DIP
  high, run the popover's full width inside its border, and carry no radius,
  so a hovered row is a `surface.raisedHover` band across the panel (lighter
  than the menu in dark mode, never sunk into it). A row has no focus state of
  its own: the keyboard's row is drawn as the hovered one, never with the
  outside focus ring, which would stick out past the popover's edge.
- Reserve 16–24 DIP radii for onboarding and marketing, not the main application shell.

Avoid web-only assumptions such as oversized controls, blur-heavy or glass surfaces, fixed physical pixels, and platform-specific fonts.

## Components and states

Use the existing native component density and Lucide `v1.47.0` SVG artwork for generic functional icons. Pin the artwork in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons` and use the same SVG geometry in the design artifacts, the React pages, and the native shell; a package or plugin alone is not the cross-surface source of truth. Keep the JusPrin mark and product-specific symbols custom. Functional clarity comes before logo-derived decoration.

- Functional icons: Lucide artwork at 16, 20, or 24 DIP, colored through the surrounding semantic token, with PNG fallback when the platform path requires it. Do not create a separate UI component for each glyph.
- Setup card (the design system's `PinnedSetupCard`; the "JusPrin v2" canvas, page "Current Setup Card", decided 2026-10-26): the band docked under the chat header, the one place in the Agent pane that is always now. Two parts. Above a 1 DIP `border.subtle` rule, the words someone wrote: the person's purpose in Body Bold, wrapping to two lines and then clipped (the whole of it in the tooltip), and the agent's plan headline in Body Small, `text.primary`; each is present only once written, and with neither the section and its rule are absent, with nothing standing in for them (not the preset name, not the project name, not a hint). Below the rule, OrcaSlicer's facts: the process and first filament presets with "N settings changed" (the project's differences from the presets and the objects' own settings) in Body Small, `text.secondary`, wrapping to two lines and then clipped like the purpose (decided 2026-10-26: at the pane's default width a Bambu preset name with a count overflows one line), and the "All settings" Button/Link, in Body Small Bold, on its first line's baseline; then the time, material and plate figures in Body Small Bold, or the one line that stands in for them ("Not sliced yet" with a Compute estimates link, "Time & material estimates recomputing…"). The eyebrow is "Setup summary" in Label Bold, `action.primary`; the only state beside it is "Agent working". A saved chat's card is the same card in `text.secondary` with the eyebrow "Earlier setup" or "Saved sliced snapshot", a quiet state such as "Saved Oct 3, 10:42" and a footnote line.
- Setup card warnings: a warning is only an annotation of the one line it contradicts, drawn directly under it, one per line: the 14 DIP `triangle-alert` glyph in `status.warning` beside Body Small text in `text.primary`. The three in use: what moved since the plan was recorded, in words the person and the model both read ("Filament changed to Generic ABS by hand", "Wall loops changed to 5 by hand", "Rename Object undone by hand", "An earlier model version was restored"; "Plan needs another look" when the host gave no reason), with a Check plan link that sends "Check the plan against what changed." in the person's name, under the plan (the app's mark after an edit that was not the agent's, cleared only by the agent recording the plan again; a setup switch stays the named reason over the setting edits after it), "Printer last reported <material>" under the presets, and "Previous estimates · not current" with a Recompute link under the estimates. A warning that names no line of the card is not the card's: print issues belong to the canvas and the chat; a mismatch between the selection and the connected machine (its nozzle, its model, what it has loaded) belongs to the chat and to the send dialog, never to the chip (see Header chip). Moments of change ("Updated", the last step with Undo, an estimate before and after, an edit by hand, "Confirmed") are the timeline rows', never the card's.
- Setup card fact glyphs: 14 DIP from `component.setupCard.iconSize`, the one size below the icon scale. The clock, material, plate and warning glyphs sit inside a row of Label text, and a 16 DIP glyph makes that row taller than its text. Do not use this size on another surface; it is not a step of the icon scale.
- Agent message box: one box with the `medium` radius, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` inside stroke, and `component.composer` insets (8 DIP padding, 4 DIP between staged files, the field, and the toolbar). The field is Body with a 4 DIP inset; it grows a line at a time up to `component.composer.maxLines` (8) and then scrolls, while the toolbar stays visible: the 32 DIP + icon button on the left, Send (`button.primarySmall`, 28 DIP) or Stop (`button.secondarySmall`, 28 DIP) on the right. While the field has the focus the whole box carries the 2 DIP `border.focus` ring. In the app, each + menu choice opens the operating system's file dialog through the host, filtered to that kind. The printer chat's + menu offers only Photo or image and Document (PDF), since it has no project for a 3D model to go into. After + come the model and thinking pickers (`button.picker`: 24 DIP, Label, a chevron), which open upward menus no narrower than `component.popover.width`: the model menu lists each set-up provider's models under the provider's name when there is more than one (a provider is added from the Agent settings); the thinking menu lists only the levels the chosen model accepts and is left out when it accepts none. A choice belongs to the chat and applies from its next turn. When the full labels do not fit beside + and Send (the composer measures them, so this follows the labels, not a breakpoint), the thinking picker drops "Thinking:" and shows the level alone; if that still does not fit, the model's name is cut with an ellipsis. Both keep their full name as the accessible name and the tooltip. A model menu of more than 12 models opens with the focus in a Field/Search (`component.fieldSearch`: 38 DIP, `small` radius, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` stroke that becomes 2 DIP `border.strong` with the focus) inset 8 DIP from the menu's sides; the menu is then `component.popover.width` wide and its rows scroll under the field. Typing filters on the model or provider name, ignoring case, the first match carries the menu-row hover fill, Up and Down move it, Enter picks it, and Escape clears the field before it closes the menu. A provider with more than 12 models shows its count beside its name while nothing is typed.
- All settings panel (the "JusPrin v2" canvas, page "Current Setup Card", the four "All settings" boards): opened from the "All settings" link at the end of the setup card's presets line, it takes the Agent pane's place under a header of the compact icon button back to the chat, the title in Body Bold and the pane's own toggle. A "Showing" row holds the design system's Select (`component.select`: 26 DIP, `small` radius, Body text, a 16 DIP chevron, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` stroke that strengthens on hover and becomes the focus ring when open; its menu is the Menu/Popover under its left edge, as wide as the field) listing the whole project, each plate when there are two or more, and each object; it follows the selection in the 3D view. Under it a Field/Search ("Search settings") beside an All / Changed Segmented Control. The presets in use sit in a `surface.subtle` box with the `medium` radius, each filament slot with its Swatch (`component.swatch`, 24 DIP, `small` radius, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` inside stroke). Groups are OrcaSlicer's own pages (Quality, Strength, Speed, Support, Multimaterial, Others, then Filament and Printer) with a 32 DIP header row (16 DIP chevron, Body Small Bold name, Label summary at the right) and rows indented 24 DIP: Body Small name and value on a 28 DIP line, a changed value in Body Small Bold with "Preset: …" in Metadata under it. Two or three filament slots stand side by side, one column per slot; more than three go through a slot picker, one at a time. The host reads the whole table in one message (`settings_catalog`, the `all_settings` capability). Only one object's view has anything to press: a Button/Link at the end of a row's note, under the value, where the table marks one — "Use project value" under a setting the object, a part, a modifier or a height range sets itself (not a range's own layer height or filament, which define it), and "Remove" under its support blockers or enforcers. - Choice control: minimum 100×32 DIP, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.

The chip makes no claim about the physical machine: what is loaded, which plate is on, which nozzle is fitted, whether it is connected or busy. Those belong to the chat, the setup card's line annotations, the printer menu's first row, and the send dialog. The chat never changes the chip.   2. Would the chip's plain text mislead without it? If not, it is a warning, and warnings go to the chat.

## Accessibility

- Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; 3:1 is allowed only for large text.
- Essential control boundaries and state indicators require 3:1.
- Keyboard focus uses a visible 2 DIP ring and may not rely on a fill-color change alone.
- Orbit on White measures 12.07:1 in the source design system.
- Bloom on Ink measures 6.62:1.
- Light secondary text measures 6.89:1 on White.
- Dark secondary text measures 10.95:1 on Ink.

## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
   retired): the Design System
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). The canvas
   frozen on 2026-10-27 (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v)
   is history, not a source. Change the token file to match, or, when the
   code's value is the one to keep, change the artifact first. Do not trust
   old commit messages about either.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.

## Typography

Product UI uses fonts already shipped by OrcaSlicer:

- HarmonyOS Sans SC Regular for body and controls.
- HarmonyOS Sans SC Bold for hierarchy and actions.
- NanumGothic for Korean and Sarabun for Thai where the existing application requires them.
- The system GUI font as fallback.
- The system monospace font only for code: API keys, file paths, commands, config text, and IDs such as hashes. Never for names, words, or measurements.

HarmonyOS Sans SC draws every digit at the same width, so times, percentages,
and other values that change in place do not shift in the UI face; they do
not need the monospace one. In the native shell only the About window's

## Layout and geometry

Design for a dense, native, high-DPI desktop application on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Use device-independent pixels (DIP), not physical pixels. Verify 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling.

- Spacing scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, and 48 DIP, plus a 2 DIP half step (`dimension.space["0.5"]`) used only for the gap between a row's main line and the detail line under it, as in a report finding or a canvas caption.
- The radius scale carries the design system's names (`dimension.radius`):
  - `small`, 4 DIP: standard controls (secondary and icon buttons, fields, the segmented control), matching OrcaSlicer's own controls.
  - `medium`, 8 DIP: containers (cards, popovers, chat bubbles) and the primary button, the one branded action.
  - `large`, 12 DIP: sheets, large dialogs and window actions.
  - `chip`, 4 DIP: the printer and filament chip in the header.
  - `full`, 14 DIP: capsule ends of anything up to 28 DIP tall: reply choices, status chips and progress tracks. A shorter box keeps a full capsule, because a radius larger than half the height is drawn as half of it.
- Menus follow the design system's Menu/Popover and Menu/Row: the popover has 8 DIP
  vertical padding, a 1 DIP border and 2 DIP between rows; rows are 36 DIP
  high, run the popover's full width inside its border, and carry no radius,
  so a hovered row is a `surface.raisedHover` band across the panel (lighter
  than the menu in dark mode, never sunk into it). A row has no focus state of
  its own: the keyboard's row is drawn as the hovered one, never with the
  outside focus ring, which would stick out past the popover's edge.
- Reserve 16–24 DIP radii for onboarding and marketing, not the main application shell.

Avoid web-only assumptions such as oversized controls, blur-heavy or glass surfaces, fixed physical pixels, and platform-specific fonts.

- Plates / Project pane: 200 DIP wide on `surface.subtle`, a 12 DIP band above a 36 DIP tab strip (the active tab is Label Bold with a 2 DIP `action.primary` rule; the other is Label in `text.secondary`). Plate rows are 32 DIP, object rows 36 DIP, both on `surface.canvas` blocks with the standard radius and a 2 DIP gap; a folded plate adds a 20 DIP Metadata summary line indented 32 DIP. Every number is under `component.leftPane`, taken from the boards on the canvas's Plates & Project Pane page.
- Agent-pane divider: transparent 8 DIP pointer target with a centered 2 DIP line; the line changes from subtle to strong on hover and to the primary action color while dragging.
- Agent-pane width: minimum 320 DIP; its maximum follows the window width while preserving at least 320 DIP for the workspace.
- Printer setup, connecting, printer settings, and filament settings help use the same temporary conversation layer over the originating workspace. The underlying Home, Prepare, or Preview screen stays selected and constructed so closing returns to it. The conversation keeps the centered content width from `component.printerSetup.contentWidth` under a window-wide header; manual settings remain available from that header. The saved project Agent pane remains a separate persistent conversation.
- Back and close (the canvas's Main Page, "Back and close", decided 2026-11-10). Each kind of going back looks different, so a person can tell a way off the screen from a step back inside a panel:
  - Home has no way back. Its header is the lockup alone.
  - Leaving a screen (the project, Print history): a 32 DIP `button.icon` with a 1 DIP `border.subtle` inside stroke and the 16 DIP Lucide `arrow-left`, at the window's top left, then 12 DIP to the screen's own title in Body Bold. The project screen's title is the project name, followed 8 DIP later by its save state in Body `text.secondary` (Saved, Saving…, or Couldn't save in `status.danger`). The tooltip names where it goes ("Back to Home").
  - A chat that fills the window for one task closes with the same outlined button holding `x`, then the task as its title: "Add a printer", "Connect <printer>", "<printer> settings" for Ask AI about printer settings, "<filament> settings" for Ask AI about filament settings. The tooltip names where it returns to when the app knows it ("Back to Prepare").
  - Going back inside a panel (a chat to the chat list, All settings, the Project tab's Details and Version history, an AI tool's setup steps): a 26 DIP `chevron-left` with no stroke in `text.secondary`, then the view's own title. The title is never part of the button.
  - A header menu's sub-list keeps its first row as its way back.
- Agent-pane collapse: an icon button in the header, left of the overflow button, whose glyph fills its right-hand column while the pane is open and empties it while the pane is closed. Double-clicking the divider closes the pane. Dragging it does not: a drag only sizes the pane and stops at its 320 DIP minimum, so aiming for a narrow pane never takes the conversation off the screen. There is no keyboard shortcut, no animation, and no automatic reopening; the pane is hidden, never destroyed, so its conversation survives. Reopening restores the width it last held.

Every interactive component must define normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focused, success, warning, and error states where relevant. Status must combine color with an icon and plain-language label.

## Accessibility

- Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; 3:1 is allowed only for large text.
- Essential control boundaries and state indicators require 3:1.
- Keyboard focus uses a visible 2 DIP ring and may not rely on a fill-color change alone.
- Orbit on White measures 12.07:1 in the source design system.
- Bloom on Ink measures 6.62:1.
- Light secondary text measures 6.89:1 on White.
- Dark secondary text measures 10.95:1 on Ink.

## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
   retired): the Design System
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). The canvas
   frozen on 2026-10-27 (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v)
   is history, not a source. Change the token file to match, or, when the
   code's value is the one to keep, change the artifact first. Do not trust
   old commit messages about either.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before

endif()
if (NOT JUSPRIN_NPM)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "npm not found. Node.js is required to build the JusPrin Agent and Home pages "
                        "(or configure with -DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF and supply the bundles yourself).")
endif()

set(_jusprin_web_shared_inputs
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json)
file(GLOB_RECURSE _jusprin_web_shared_glob CONFIGURE_DEPENDS
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../WebShared/*
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/jusprin/ui/icons/*)
list(APPEND _jusprin_web_shared_inputs ${_jusprin_web_shared_glob})

# Any further arguments are folders of another page whose source this page
# imports, so a change there rebuilds this bundle too.
function(jusprin_web_bundle name project_dir output)
    file(GLOB_RECURSE _src CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${project_dir}/src/*)
    foreach(_imported ${ARGN})
        file(GLOB_RECURSE _imported_src CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${_imported}/*)
        list(APPEND _src ${_imported_src})
    endforeach()
    set(_stamp ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${name}-node_modules.stamp)
    # npm ci writes node_modules/.package-lock.json. Listing it as OUTPUT
    # means deleting node_modules retriggers the install; the stamp in the
    # build tree is what the bundle command depends on.
    set(_modules ${project_dir}/node_modules/.package-lock.json)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${_stamp} ${_modules}
        COMMAND ${JUSPRIN_NPM} ci --no-audit --no-fund
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch ${_stamp}
        DEPENDS ${project_dir}/package.json ${project_dir}/package-lock.json
        WORKING_DIRECTORY ${project_dir}
        COMMENT "npm ci (${name})"
        VERBATIM)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${output}
        COMMAND ${JUSPRIN_NPM} run build
        DEPENDS ${_stamp} ${_src} ${_jusprin_web_shared_inputs}
                ${project_dir}/index.html ${project_dir}/vite.config.ts ${project_dir}/tsconfig.json
        WORKING_DIRECTORY ${project_dir}
        COMMENT "vite build (${name}) -> ${output}"
        VERBATIM)
endfunction()

jusprin_web_bundle(agent ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../AgentUI ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/jusprin/agent/index.html)
# Home's first launch draws the Agent page's add-printer form.
jusprin_web_bundle(home  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../HomeUI  ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/jusprin/home/index.html
                   ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../AgentUI/src)

add_custom_target(jusprin_web ALL DEPENDS
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/jusprin/agent/index.html
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/jusprin/home/index.html)
add_dependencies(OrcaSlicer jusprin_web)

---
name: agent-panel-css-namespaces
description: AgentUI styles.css has no CSS modules — the setup-* class prefix belongs to the agent setup screens, so new components need their own prefix
metadata:
  type: project
---

`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css` is one flat global stylesheet
with no CSS modules or scoping. The `setup-*` prefix is already taken by the
agent **setup screens** (`Setup.tsx`, `SetupLocalTool.tsx`) — `.setup-card`
there is `display: flex; flex-direction: column` on a lavender
`--surface-selected` ground.

**Why:** a new component that reuses one of those names silently inherits
`display: flex` and leaks its own rules back onto the setup screens. This cost
real time once: the "Current setup" card reused `.setup-card`, which defeated
its `white-space: nowrap` title clamp and re-tinted its background. Both
suites stayed green — jsdom does no layout, so no unit test can see it.

**How to apply:** pick a prefix that does not already appear in styles.css
(`grep -n '^\.<prefix>' src/styles.css`), and verify layout by rendering the
real component at real width rather than trusting tests. The pattern that
works: `SetupCard.preview.test.tsx` uses `renderToStaticMarkup` plus the real
styles.css and design tokens to emit a page of every state, served over a
local http server and measured in the browser (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`,
row heights). See [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

"""Screenshot canvas boards with the canvas's own Design Component runtime, so <dc-import> boards render whole
(render.py draws them blank). Serves <project dir> on a local port with ./support.js = the runtime saved from the
artifact's artifact-type/dc-runtime.js and /_blob/<id> mapped by blobs.json, then runs headless Chrome with its own
--user-data-dir. Usage: render_dc.py <work dir holding project/ and runtime/> <out dir> [--dark] <board.dc.html>..."""
import functools, http.server, json, re, socketserver, subprocess, sys, tempfile, threading
from pathlib import Path
args = sys.argv[1:]
dark = '--dark' in args
if dark: args.remove('--dark')
work, out, names = Path(args[0]), Path(args[1]), args[2:]
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
proj, runtime = work / 'project', work / 'runtime'
blobs = json.loads((runtime / 'blobs.json').read_text()) if (runtime / 'blobs.json').exists() else {}
chrome = '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome'
class H(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def translate_path(self, path):
        p = path.split('?')[0]
        if p.endswith('/support.js'): return str(runtime / 'dc-runtime.js')
        if p.startswith('/_blob/'):
            b = blobs.get(p[7:])
            if b: return str(runtime / b)
        return super().translate_path(path)
    def do_GET(self):
        # --dark: the board's theme prop defaults to dark, the way the canvas's Theme switch sets it.
        if dark and self.path.split('?')[0].endswith('.dc.html') and 'board=1' in self.path:
            s = Path(self.translate_path(self.path)).read_text()
            s = s.replace('"theme":{"editor":"enum","options":["light","dark"],"default":"light"}', '"theme":{"editor":"enum","options":["light","dark"],"default":"dark"}')
            b = s.encode(); self.send_response(200); self.send_header('Content-Type', 'text/html; charset=utf-8'); self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(b))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b); return
        return super().do_GET()
srv = socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), functools.partial(H, directory=str(proj)))
srv.daemon_threads = True
threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
port = srv.server_address[1]
for name in names:
    s = (proj / name).read_text()
    m = re.search(r'"\$preview":\{"width":(\d+),"height":(\d+)\}', s)
    w, h = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    png = out / (name.replace('.dc.html', '') + ('-dark' if dark else '') + '.png')
    subprocess.run([chrome, '--headless=new', '--disable-gpu', '--no-first-run', f'--user-data-dir={tempfile.mkdtemp()}', '--hide-scrollbars', f'--window-size={w},{h}', '--force-device-scale-factor=2',

def copy_pictures(area, entry, out):
    """Copies the run's pictures the page uses: "name.png": "the run's file",
    or {"from": "the run's file", "crop": [left, top, right, bottom]} to keep
    part of it, in the file's own pixels. Returns the names it could not."""
    from PIL import Image, ImageChops  # only this step needs it

    missing = []
    for name, wanted in entry.get("pictures", {}).items():
        wanted = {"from": wanted} if isinstance(wanted, str) else wanted
        made = out / wanted["from"]
        if not made.is_file() or made.stat().st_size == 0:
            missing.append(f"{name} (the run wrote no {wanted['from']})")
            continue
        picture = Image.open(made).convert("RGB")
        if "crop" in wanted:
            picture = picture.crop(tuple(wanted["crop"]))
        # One flat colour is a capture the screen refused, not a picture of the app.
        if picture.getextrema() == tuple((low, low) for low, _ in picture.getextrema()):
            missing.append(f"{name} ({wanted['from']} is blank: see this script's note on Screen Recording)")
            continue
        target = PICTURES / area / name
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        # An unchanged picture is left alone, so a run that changes nothing changes no file.
        if target.is_file() and not ImageChops.difference(Image.open(target).convert("RGB"), picture).getbbox() \
                and Image.open(target).size == picture.size:
            continue
        picture.save(target, optimize=True)
    return missing
